data.content_ref: inline:The target's central distinction—'safe' = a design-time intent contract and 'idempotent' = an observed runtime/behavioral property—is not the published RFC 9110 distinction it is asked to draw on. RFC 9110 defines idempotence in terms of the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests being the same as for one request, not in terms of 'observable result'; and 'safe' is also a semantic/intended-effect property ('essentially read-only' defined semantics), while explicitly permitting side effects. Because the target frames idempotence as observable-result equivalence, its claim that safe ⊂ idempotent via 'no-effect trivially satisfies behavioral equivalence' is unsupported: a safe method may still have non-repeat-equivalent side effects under the target's own runtime criterion. Thus it fails the problem's demand for a precise, definition-grounded distinction between the two terms.
